"source" is just a variable name (an identifier). The line

const source = items.filter(Boolean);

means: call items.filter(...) and assign the returned array to a constant named source.

What filter(Boolean) does:
- Array.prototype.filter expects a predicate function. Passing the built-in Boolean function causes each element to be coerced to true/false.
- Elements that coerce to true (truthy) are kept; elements that coerce to false (falsy) are removed.
- Falsy values in JavaScript: false, 0, "", null, undefined, and NaN.

So source will be a new array containing only the truthy elements from items.

Notes:
- const means the binding source cannot be reassigned, but the array object it refers to can be mutated (e.g., source.push(...)).
- If items is not an array (or doesn't have filter), this will throw an error.

Example:
const items = [0, 1, "", "hello", null, undefined, 42];
const source = items.filter(Boolean); // => [1, "hello", 42]
